newsitem.title: USA: Russia wheat flour imports 750,000 tonnes - attache.
newsitem.headline: Russia wheat flour imports 750,000 tonnes - attache.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache pegged 1996/97 and 1997/98 Russia wheat flour imports at about 750,000, after peaking at 900,000 tonnes during 1995/96.
In a report dated April 1 that was released in Washington Thursday, the attache said the slightly lower import level was due to small increases in domestic production.

The attache also said corn demand in Russia may be on the upswing after a sharp drop since the Soviet Union's breakup. The attache said a few Russian poultry producers are starting to make a come back, and the industry may have bottomed out in its decline.
"In three to five years, at present very small imports of 150,000 tons could rebound and even double in 1998/99 provided Russia's currently fragile economy can maintain itself," the attache wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
